item.title: Performance
item.description:
The PPTX figures below are for v0.5.0 and the vector PDF figures for v0.4.0. The first table is for v0.3.0, the previous release, which renders slides concurrently and parses its fonts once (go-slides/slides#11).

The 100-slide PDF and PPTX rows of the three tables below were measured before v0.18.0. They were re-measured with v0.26.1 once the regression tracked in go-slides/slides#117 was fixed: see Several cores.

go-slides and marp-cli 4.5.1 were run as subprocesses on the same decks, on an Apple M4 Max (16 CPUs) with a 1-minute load average under 8, five interleaved rounds after a warm-up. Time is the median wall time; memory is the peak of the whole process tree (marp-cli drives a Chrome, whose processes count).

Measured with v0.3.0 on all cores (16 CPUs).

Deck Output go-slides marp-cli go-slides memory marp-cli memory
100 slides HTML 36 ms 315 ms 47 MiB 140 MiB
100 slides PDF 1.14 s 1.88 s 242 MiB 1,509 MiB
100 slides PNG, every slide 0.97 s 5.44 s 225 MiB 1,354 MiB
100 slides PPTX 3.39 s 8.03 s 530 MiB 1,373 MiB
gaia, 20 slides PDF 283 ms 1.57 s 154 MiB 1,315 MiB
math and code, 20 slides PNG, every slide 250 ms 2.32 s 168 MiB 1,286 MiB

Vector PDF

In v0.4.0 the PDF is drawn as vectors (see Command line). Same machine and method, 2026-10-19:

Measured with v0.4.0 on all cores (16 CPUs), on 2026-10-19.

Deck go-slides marp-cli v0.3.0 go-slides size marp-cli size v0.3.0 size
100 slides 306 ms 1,763 ms 1,147 ms 758 KiB 837 KiB 10.0 MiB
gaia, 20 slides 93 ms 1,546 ms 285 ms 32 KiB 66 KiB 582 KiB
math and code, 20 slides 140 ms 1,643 ms 294 ms 124 KiB 335 KiB 638 KiB

Memory for the 100-slide PDF: 158 MiB, against 1,512 MiB for marp-cli; CPU time 0.9 s against 2.7 s.

The v0.4.0 figures for the 100-slide PDF were measured on 2026-10-19 at 21:29, with a 1-minute load average of 7.7, over three rounds: go-slides 306 ms, 758 KiB and 158 MiB; marp-cli 1,838 ms, 837 KiB and 1,512 MiB.

Editable PPTX

Since v0.5.0 the PPTX is made of text boxes, shapes and pictures (see Command line). Measured on 2026-10-19 at 22:51, with a 1-minute load average of 7.1, over three rounds:

Measured with v0.5.0 on all cores (16 CPUs), on 2026-10-19.

Deck go-slides marp-cli go-slides size marp-cli size go-slides memory marp-cli memory
100 slides 348 ms 7,795 ms 760 KiB 7.2 MiB 204 MiB 1,370 MiB
gaia, 20 slides 112 ms 4,608 ms 893 KiB 4.8 MiB
math and code, 20 slides 207 ms 2,780 ms 842 KiB 1.5 MiB

For the 100-slide deck, v0.4.0 took 4.7 s, 4.8 MiB and 540 MiB. marp-cli’s PPTX holds pictures. Most of an editable deck’s size is the embedded fonts.

Several cores

Measured with v0.26.1 (go-webengine/engine v0.48.0): wall time in ms with 1, 2, 4 and 16 cores, against marp-cli. The 1-minute load average was 5.7 at the start. marp-cli’s time does not change with the number of cores, because its -P only spreads separate files across browsers. slidesbench -cores produces this table. go-slides is faster than marp-cli on every row, at every core count.

Deck, mode 1 core 2 4 16 marp-cli
100 slides, PNG 2628 1397 899 766 5197
gaia, 20 slides, PNG 731 394 227 222 2331
math and code, 20 slides, PNG 600 333 199 192 2140
gaia, 20 slides, PDF 85 64 57 58 1411
math and code, 20 slides, PDF 278 183 139 135 1457
gaia, 20 slides, PPTX 99 77 69 70 3110
math and code, 20 slides, PPTX 395 268 189 179 2527
100 slides, PDF 544 331 247 256 1534
100 slides, PPTX 692 435 317 276 7248

Fixed in v0.26.1. From v0.18.0 to v0.26.0 the 100-slide PDF was slower than marp-cli, and the 100-slide PDF and PPTX did not scale with cores: the engine rebuilt the variable-font instances for every page. go-webengine/engine v0.48.0 shares them across pages (go-webengine/engine#443), and v0.26.1 picks it up: the 100-slide PDF takes 544 ms on one core instead of 3166 ms, with a peak of 169 MiB instead of 2182 MiB, and is 792.4 KiB instead of 1005.5 KiB, because the font is embedded 3 times instead of 102. The pages are pixel-identical. It was reported in go-slides/slides#117 (closed).

Why it is fast

  • No browser to start. marp-cli launches Chrome for every PDF, image and PPTX export; go-slides renders with go-webengine inside its own process.
  • Slides render in parallel, four at a time by default, and each image is written as soon as it is its turn: a long deck is never held in memory as images.
  • Fonts are parsed once per process, not once per slide.

What it does not win

  • PDF size, in v0.3.0. Each slide was an image in the PDF: 10 MiB against 837 KiB for the 100-slide deck. The vector PDF above is smaller than marp-cli’s.
  • CPU time on big decks. Four workers spend more CPU than the wall time shows: in v0.3.0, 3.2 s against marp-cli’s 2.7 s for the 100-slide PDF (0.9 s for the vector PDF).
  • Memory is an upper bound for marp-cli: Chrome’s processes share pages that the sum counts in each. Its largest single process is 220–320 MiB.

The method, every deck and mode, and the commands to reproduce the figures are in BENCHMARKS.md.
